parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented facility, custody, border or police exposure, and no record of anti-trans violence — the visitor-facing axes are largely free of documented restriction. Positives: pride marches proceeded without impediment, an LGBT drop-in centre opened, health ethics bar discrimination, and broadcast rules limit incitement. Sodomy law is a dead-letter secondary factor (unused since 1990, decriminalised 2024). Weighing against: organized political hostility, contested decriminalisation implementation, a court-enforcement gap showing institutions not reliably working for LGBT people, absent equality legislation naming gender identity, 2009 psychology rules still pathologizing gender identity, and thin data outside two cities. The enforcement gap chiefly concerns marriage/residency, not short visits. Net: acceptance documented but protections thin and remedies unreliable — reduced risk with real friction.
